events.title: Supreme Court Revises Rules of Procedure
events.summary: The Supreme Court of the United States issued an order revising its Rules of Procedure, which will take effect on March 16, 2026. The revised rules will replace those promulgated on December 5, 2022, which will be rescinded as of March 15, 2026. The new rules will govern all proceedings after their effective date, except in cases where their application would be infeasible or unjust, in which case the former rules will apply.
events.why_relevant: The revision of the Supreme Court's procedural rules affects how cases are managed and decided, impacting the administration of justice.

events.title: SCOTUS grants Solicitor General's motion in Montgomery v. Caribe Transport II
events.summary: The Supreme Court of the United States granted the motion of the Solicitor General to participate in oral argument as amicus curiae and for divided argument in the case of Montgomery v. Caribe Transport II, LLC, et al. This procedural decision allows the Solicitor General to present the government's perspective during the oral arguments, potentially influencing the Court's understanding of the case.
events.why_relevant: The participation of the Solicitor General as amicus curiae can impact the Court's deliberations and the outcome of the case.

events.title: Supreme Court releases opinion in Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump (24-1287)
events.summary: The Supreme Court released an official slip opinion in Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump. Docket number(s): 24-1287.
events.why_relevant: The Supreme Court's official opinion in Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump is a primary legal source. Supreme Court opinions can define binding national law and alter the legal position of the executive branch, federal agencies, states, litigants, and democratic institutions.
